topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its core learning objectives.

topics.label: Traditional cancer therapies and drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine conventional therapeutic modalities—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with the associated systemic toxicity and efflux-mediated drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer-specific vulnerabilities and checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss therapeutic strategies designed to exploit intrinsic tumor weaknesses, including hormone dependence, checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Kinase-targeted therapies and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on the design of small-molecule kinase inhibitors and the molecular mechanisms that lead to bypass signaling, acquired resistance, and drug addiction.

topics.label: Antibody-based therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the therapeutic use of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to selectively target cancer cell-surface proteins.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess natural immune surveillance and examine therapeutic approaches that engage or engineer the immune system to eliminate tumors.

topics.label: Challenges, historical progress, and future perspectives in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate overall mortality trends, clinical complexities, and future therapeutic paradigms across oncology.
